subject: NimbleAI Dedicated SKU blend & scaling playbook
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbleai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbleai.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance — workload profile attached

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As mentioned, we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for an upcoming production launch (main product: interactive summarization + conversational assistant). We attached a small workload profile (nimble_workload_profile.csv) — the important bits:~
- 70% short requests (<128 tokens) with p95 latency target ~130ms
- 20% medium (~512 tokens) with p95 target ~250ms
- 10% long context (2k-8k tokens) used by our research flows; p95 tolerable up to ~600ms but very cost sensitive
- Typical QPS: steady 200 qps during business hours, burst 900 qps for 20-40 minute windows
- KV cache expected to hit ~18% for conversational flows after rollout

We need recommendations for a Dedicated SKU mix (H100/A100/L4) and a pilot sizing plan (what to reserve vs burst). Cost sensitivity: we prefer lower unit cost for short/medium paths; SLA: 99.9% availability, 200ms p95 for core endpoint (short-only).

Can you share a short playbook (runbook + suggested fleet mix) and what benchmarking you need from our side?

Attachments: nimble_workload_profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Thanks,
Elena
VP Product, NimbleAI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbleai.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbleai.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance — workload profile attached

Elena — thanks, this is perfect context. High-level recommendation first, then an actionable pilot plan and what we need to benchmark.

Quick summary recommendation (pilot -> committed):
- Pilot (4 weeks): 2 x A100 nodes + 6 x L4 nodes (as burstable on Dedicated) — covers medium and short paths for functional SLO validation and latency profiling.
- Committed mix (initial reserve): 30% A100, 60% L4, 10% H100 by slot count. Rationale below.

Why this mix (short version):
- L4: best tokens/$ for short requests and high QPS; low latency for <128 token flows and fast cold-starts. Use L4 as the default route for your core endpoint (70% traffic).
- A100: mid-point for medium-context 512 tokens with better memory headroom than L4; significantly cheaper than H100 while meeting p95 targets for most medium queries. Good for batching and efficient KV cache use.
- H100: reserved for long-context jobs (2k-8k) and heavy multi-turn research endpoints that need larger memory and NVLink bandwidth; also used as a fallthrough when A100 nodes face memory pressure.

Detailed sizing notes and numbers (rough starting point):
- Steady baseline (200 qps): assume token mix yields ~30k tokens/sec. With our observed throughputs: 1 L4 slot ~handles ~350 short qps equivalent; 1 A100 ~handles ~900 medium qps equivalent with moderate batching; 1 H100 ~handles 1.8k long-context-equivalent throughput when heavily batched.
- For your 200 steady qps dominated by short contexts, 6 L4 slots is a conservative start (handles steady + buffer). The 2 A100s in pilot handle medium flows and provide an ops safety net.
- For burst windows (900 qps): use burst pool that includes additional L4s and leverage autoscaling burst credits; recommend we configure 12 L4 burst slots in your Dedicated pool (can be burst-only, pay-as-you-go).

Cost-economics:
- Expect tokens/$ to be lowest on L4 for short paths; A100 offers best marginal improvement for medium contexts before H100's premium kicks in. Keep H100 fraction small and only route long-context/resiliency traffic to it.

Operational levers we will apply:
- Prefix/KV caching: prioritize caching for conversation paths to raise KV hit-rate from 18% -> target 35% after warmup; this directly reduces H100 and A100 pressure.
- Smart routing: route by latency SLO + token length. Short endpoint -> L4; medium -> A100; long -> H100 (with fallback to A100 for degraded cases).
- Canary config: start with 10% traffic on A100 for medium route during the first week, increase as metrics stabilize.

Pilot plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0: Benchmarking. Redwood runs perf tests against your anonymized workload sample (we need 24h sample of requests + 50 synthetic long-context cases).
- Week 1: Deploy pilot pool (2 A100, 6 L4). Run production-mirroring for short path + small percent of real traffic. Collect p95 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, KV hit rates.
- Week 2: Adjust batching/quantization profiles; test cold starts and tail latencies, tune autoscale policies.
- Week 3: Route medium traffic progressively (10% -> 50% -> 100% medium route as p95 holds).
- Week 4: Evaluate cost vs latency; propose reserve commitment level and SKU mix for Dedicated.

What we need from you for benchmarking:
- 24-hour anonymized request log (timestamp, token_count, endpoint, avg_response_ms) — if possible, the CSV you attached already helps.
- Example long-context documents (5-10) for end-to-end profiling (2k-8k tokens).
- Targeted SLOs per endpoint (you gave these, but a formal doc helps).

Attachments from Redwood: redwood_sku_playbook.pdf (playbook + suggested autoscale policies + cost model). I'll drop a small spreadsheet with modeled slot counts after the benchmarking run.

Next steps if this sounds good:
1) Can you confirm you can share a 24-hour anonymized request log by Monday?
2) Would you like a short call (30m) tomorrow to walk through the pilot runbook and timelines?

I'll loop Irene for ops constraints and Ben for pricing/commit terms.

Thanks,

Adding some ops constraints and a couple of runbook items we should include before the pilot goes live:

Ops constraints to validate during pilot:
- NVLink topology: if we place H100 heavily, confirm network topology for multi-GPU models (some long-context kernels assume NVLink for checkpointing). If your long-context workloads are single-GPU-friendly, we can compress H100 needs.
- Memory fragmentation: long-lived KV caches can fragment memory on A100; we'll monitor allocation churn and may suggest periodic soft restarts for A100 nodes.
- Disk-backed KV spill: for very large contexts, offer a fallback to spill to high-speed NVMe on the node rather than immediate H100 escalation.

Runbook items (we will prepare):
- Canary checklist (smoke tests, p95 guardrails, rollback thresholds).
- Autoscale thresholds for L4 burst: define CPU/GPU util and queue-length triggers.
- Fallback policy: if A100 p95 > 2x target for 3 consecutive 1-min windows, route new long-context requests to H100 only after >75% token_count threshold.

Also note pricing/commit: Ben — please draft a conservative reserve vs burst pricing slide with a recommended minimum commit (we typically push for a 3-month reserve to lock better rate for A100/H100 slots).

Irene Choi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
